# 1 Kings Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-drew-near the-days-of David to-die, and-he-commanded ʾet-Solomon his-son, saying,

**2** "I am-going in-the-way-of all the-earth. And-be-strong, and-be a-man.

**3** And-keep the-charge-of YHWH your-God, to-walk in-his-ways, to-keep his-statutes and-his-commandments and-his-judgments and-his-testimonies, as-it-is-written in-the-Torah-of Moses, so-that you-may-prosper in-all that you-do and-in-all where you-turn,

**4** so-that YHWH may-establish ʾet-his-word that he-spoke concerning-me, saying, 'If your-sons guard ʾet-their-way, to-walk before-me in-faithfulness, with-all their-heart and-with-all their-soul, saying, there-shall-not be-cut-off to-you a-man from-upon the-throne-of Israel.'

**5** And-also you know ʾet what Joab son-of Zeruiah did to-me, what he-did to-the-two commanders-of the-armies-of Israel, to-Abner son-of Ner and-to-Amasa son-of Jether — and-he-killed-them, and-he-put bloods-of war in-peace, and-he-put bloods-of war on-his-belt that was-on his-waist and-on his-sandal that was-on his-foot.

**6** And-do according-to-your-wisdom, and-do-not let-go-down his-gray-hair in-peace to-Sheol.

**7** And-to-the-sons-of Barzillai the-Gileadite do ḥesed, and-let-them-be among-those-eating at-your-table, for so they-drew-near to-me when-I-fled from-before Absalom your-brother.

**8** And-behold, with-you is Shimei son-of Gera the-Benjaminite from-Bahurim, and-he cursed-me a-grievous curse on-the-day-of my-going to-Mahanaim. And-he came-down to-meet-me at-the-Jordan, and-I-swore to-him by-YHWH, saying, 'I-will-not put-you-to-death by-the-sword.'

**9** And-now, do-not hold-him-guiltless, for a-wise man you are, and-you-will-know ʾet what you-should-do to-him, and-bring-down ʾet-his-gray-hair in-blood to-Sheol."

**10** And-David lay-down with his-fathers, and-was-buried in-the-City-of David.

**11** And-the-days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: in-Hebron he-reigned seven years, and-in-Jerusalem he-reigned thirty and-three years.

**12** And-Solomon sat upon the-throne-of David his-father, and-his-kingdom was-established greatly.

**13** And-Adonijah son-of Haggith came to-Bathsheba mother-of Solomon, and-she-said, "Is-peace your-coming?" And-he-said, "Peace."

**14** And-he-said, "A-word to-me to-you." And-she-said, "Speak."

**15** And-he-said, "You know that to-me was the-kingdom, and-upon-me set all-Israel their-faces to-reign. But-the-kingdom turned-around and-became my-brother's, for from-YHWH it-was his.

**16** And-now, one petition I am-asking from-you; do-not turn-away ʾet-my-face." And-she-said to-him, "Speak."

**17** And-he-said, "Say, please, to-Solomon the-king — for he-will-not turn-away ʾet-your-face — that-he-give to-me ʾet-Abishag the-Shunammite as-a-wife."

**18** And-Bathsheba said, "Good; I will-speak for-you to the-king."

**19** And-Bathsheba came to the-king Solomon, to-speak to-him concerning Adonijah. And-the-king rose to-meet-her, and-bowed-down to-her, and-sat on his-throne. And-he-placed a-throne for-the-mother-of the-king, and-she-sat at-his-right.

**20** And-she-said, "One small petition I am-asking from-you; do-not turn-away ʾet-my-face." And-the-king said to-her, "Ask, my-mother, for I-will-not turn-away ʾet-your-face."

**21** And-she-said, "Let ʾet-Abishag the-Shunammite be-given to-Adonijah your-brother as-a-wife."

**22** And-the-king Solomon answered and-said to-his-mother, "And-why are-you asking ʾet-Abishag the-Shunammite for-Adonijah? Ask for-him ʾet-the-kingdom also — for he is my-brother the-older than-me — and-for-him and-for-Abiathar the-priest and-for-Joab son-of Zeruiah!"

**23** And-the-king Solomon swore by-YHWH, saying, "Thus may-God do to-me and-thus may-he-add, for against his-own-life Adonijah has-spoken ʾet-this word.

**24** And-now, as-YHWH lives, who established-me and-set-me upon the-throne-of David my-father, and-who made for-me a-house as he-spoke, for today Adonijah shall-be-put-to-death."

**25** And-the-king Solomon sent by-the-hand-of Benaiah son-of Jehoiada, and-he-struck-him, and-he-died.

**26** And-to-Abiathar the-priest the-king said, "Go to-Anathoth, to your-fields, for a-man-of death you are. But-on-this day I-will-not put-you-to-death, because you-carried ʾet-the-ark-of the-Lord YHWH before David my-father, and-because you-were-afflicted in-all that my-father was-afflicted."

**27** And-Solomon drove-out ʾet-Abiathar from-being priest to-YHWH, to-fulfill ʾet-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke concerning the-house-of Eli in-Shiloh.

**28** And-the-report came to Joab — for Joab had-turned after Adonijah, though after Absalom he-had-not turned — and-Joab fled to the-tent-of YHWH and-seized the-horns-of the-altar.

**29** And-it-was-told to-the-king Solomon that Joab had-fled to the-tent-of YHWH, and-behold, beside the-altar. And-Solomon sent ʾet-Benaiah son-of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike-him-down."

**30** And-Benaiah came to the-tent-of YHWH and-said to-him, "Thus says the-king, 'Come-out.'" And-he-said, "No, for here I-will-die." And-Benaiah brought-back ʾet-word to-the-king, saying, "Thus spoke Joab, and-thus he-answered-me."

**31** And-the-king said to-him, "Do as he-has-spoken, and-strike-him-down, and-bury-him, and-remove the-bloods-of-gratuitous-killing that Joab shed from-upon-me and-from-upon the-house-of my-father.

**32** And-YHWH will-return ʾet-his-blood upon his-own-head, who struck-down two men more-righteous and-better than-he, and-killed-them with-the-sword — and-my-father David did-not know — ʾet-Abner son-of Ner, commander-of the-army-of Israel, and-ʾet-Amasa son-of Jether, commander-of the-army-of Judah.

**33** And-their-blood will-return on-the-head-of Joab and-on-the-head-of his-seed forever. And-to-David and-to-his-seed and-to-his-house and-to-his-throne there-will-be peace forever from-YHWH."

**34** And-Benaiah son-of Jehoiada went-up, and-struck-him, and-killed-him. And-he-was-buried at-his-house in-the-wilderness.

**35** And-the-king placed ʾet-Benaiah son-of Jehoiada in-his-place over the-army, and-ʾet-Zadok the-priest the-king placed in-place-of Abiathar.

**36** And-the-king sent and-called for-Shimei, and-said to-him, "Build for-yourself a-house in-Jerusalem and-dwell there, and-do-not go-out from-there anywhere.

**37** And-it-shall-be, on-the-day you-go-out and-cross ʾet-the-brook Kidron, know surely that dying you-shall-die. Your-blood will-be on-your-own-head."

**38** And-Shimei said to-the-king, "The-word is-good. As my-lord the-king has-spoken, so your-servant will-do." And-Shimei dwelt in-Jerusalem many days.

**39** And-it-was at-the-end-of three years, and-two servants-of Shimei fled to Achish son-of Maacah, king-of Gath. And-they-told Shimei, saying, "Behold, your-servants are in-Gath."

**40** And-Shimei arose and-saddled ʾet-his-donkey, and-went to-Gath, to Achish, to-seek ʾet-his-servants. And-Shimei went and-brought ʾet-his-servants from-Gath.

**41** And-it-was-told to-Solomon that Shimei had-gone from-Jerusalem to-Gath and-had-returned.

**42** And-the-king sent and-called for-Shimei, and-said to-him, "Did-I-not make-you-swear by-YHWH, and-I-warned you, saying, 'On-the-day you-go-out and-walk anywhere, know surely that dying you-shall-die'? And-you-said to-me, 'The-word is-good; I-have-heard.'

**43** And-why did-you-not keep ʾet-the-oath-of YHWH and-ʾet-the-commandment that I-commanded upon-you?"

**44** And-the-king said to-Shimei, "You know ʾet-all the-evil that your-heart knows, that you-did to-David my-father. And-YHWH has-returned ʾet-your-evil upon your-own-head.

**45** And-the-king Solomon shall-be-blessed, and-the-throne-of David shall-be established before YHWH forever."

**46** And-the-king commanded ʾet-Benaiah son-of Jehoiada, and-he-went-out and-struck-him, and-he-died. And-the-kingdom was-established in-the-hand-of Solomon.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **2:5 — "bloods-of war in-peace" (דְּמֵי מִלְחָמָה בְּשָׁלֹם)**: The plural "bloods" intensifies the accusation. Joab shed wartime blood during peacetime — the gravity is in the category violation.

2. **2:9 — "bring-down his-gray-hair in-blood to-Sheol"**: David's deathbed instructions are chillingly specific. The gray-hair motif (used for both Joab and Shimei) suggests the debt is old and must be collected before natural death arrives.

3. **2:22 — "Ask for-him the-kingdom also"**: Solomon's explosive response reveals the political reading Bathsheba missed — requesting a king's concubine is tantamount to claiming his throne.

4. **2:27 — fulfillment of the Eli prophecy**: The narrator draws the theological line explicitly — Abiathar's removal fulfills the word spoken against Eli's house in 1 Samuel 2:27-36.

5. **2:28 — "though after Absalom he-had-not turned"**: A parenthetical clarification — Joab stayed loyal during Absalom's revolt but chose the wrong side in the Adonijah affair.

6. **2:46 — "the-kingdom was-established"**: The chapter's final word. Three executions and one exile later, Solomon's throne is secure. The Hebrew נָכוֹנָה (established/firm) echoes the Davidic covenant language.

— EMET
